topic.title: Dropped on Friday, forgotten by Wednesday
topic.claim: The show everyone binged on the weekend is forgotten by midweek, and the platform is mostly fine with that.
topic.moment: Friday it's all your group chat talks about; by Wednesday nobody remembers the lead's name.

turn.believed: A show flops when people stop talking about it.
turn.actually: Platforms often measure signups and watch hours in the first days, not how long a show stays in conversation.

topic.because: Dropping every episode at once pulls people in for one weekend. Weekly releases keep a show alive longer, which is why big shows lately come out in parts.
topic.payoff: The shows you still quote years later were almost all ones you had to wait for.
topic.behaviour: Platforms release full seasons at once; viewers binge and move on.
topic.mechanism: Platforms reward a weekend spike more than slow, lasting talk.
topic.send_to: The friend who finishes a season in one night and then has nobody to discuss it with.
topic.why_now: More big shows are switching between full drops and split releases.

score.why: Weekend binge, forgotten by Wednesday, and the platform is fine with that. It's pop culture seen from the seller's side.

topic.villain: a release strategy built for a signup spike, not lasting attention
